findings.trigger: Supervisor dies after Popen starts a worker but before the running PID lifecycle write. Lifecycle remains launch_pending with no pid. Recovery finds the worker by command and sends SIGKILL, but the only group-absence check is guarded by lifecycle.get(pid), not the discovered PID.
findings.consequence: Recovery may finalize the group and remove the new-run gate while the discovered worker/group still exists, especially with unreaped or blocked descendants. It also cannot identify a surviving descendant if the unrecorded leader has already disappeared. This is precisely the launch-record gap the new comment says is covered.
findings.suggested_correction: Retain and check all discovered worker process groups before finalization; add a durable worker startup PID/group handshake before any suite work so a leader disappearing during the parent launch gap cannot erase group identity. Do not finalize a launch_pending lifecycle until absence of every launched group is established.

findings.trigger: SIGTERM/SIGINT arrives after success has become True in the completed-result branch but before the try block finishes. The BaseException handler sets status=interrupted without resetting success.
findings.consequence: Durable completion can contain success=True and status=interrupted. finalize selects succeeded from success, marks all member attempts succeeded, and returns zero; recorder rejects the same immutable report because its status is interrupted. Recovery only repeats the inconsistent completion.
findings.suggested_correction: Keep success/status as one consistent outcome. Clear success in the interruption handler, or deliberately preserve a completed succeeded outcome with a separately recorded late signal; make finalization reject inconsistent success/status combinations.

findings.trigger: A presentation input is valid JSON but not an object, for example [] or null. Preflight only json.loads it, then ledger.update commits before checkpoint.update/conformance.update raises.
findings.consequence: A predictable invalid input still causes postcommit presentation failure even though the repair explicitly intends validation before commit. The new attachment key correctly prevents duplicate ledger transactions on retries, so this is a remaining preflight defect rather than lost evidence.
findings.suggested_correction: Require both loaded presentation inputs to be dictionaries (and any fields relied on later to have expected shape) before ledger.update.
